assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength idea with Ye's demonstration of Sr clocks at the 1e-18 level. It removes Doppler and recoil shifts while averaging over many atoms. It is precise, quantitative physics where atomic structure theory and experiment meet, and it opens relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice trapping and made the first demonstrations; Ye's group drove it to record accuracy and stability. The two-name credit is clean and natural, though Hall and Hänsch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already cover adjacent ground, and other groups (PTB, NIST, SYRTE) have contributed.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years old and independently reproduced in many laboratories, with agreement between clocks well below the old Cs standard. Recognition is timely, and the interpretation is not in doubt.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier precision-metrology prizes could weigh against it.
Whether Ye's other clock work (and the Th-229 nuclear clock) should be part of any citation is unresolved.
I have not independently verified the exact record accuracy figures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, with correlated insulators and superconductivity, were a genuinely unexpected result that sharply opened a new field of moire quantum matter. The theoretical prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald) preceded the experiment and was confirmed quantitatively. It asks real questions about strong correlations in a tunable platform.
assessment.attribution: The theory credit to Bistritzer and MacDonald and the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero (with Yuan Cao) is a coherent three-person configuration. Cao as a student, and the roles of Dean, Young, Kim and others in related moire systems, make the allocation sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Since 2018, many independent groups have reproduced the results across many devices. The mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so the field is young but the central discovery is firm.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism remains unsettled.
Possibly premature relative to a decade-scale maturity.
Excluded contributors (Cao, Dean, Young, Kim, Santos) complicate fairness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This gives a controlled way to see many-body quantum physics directly, which fits the basic question of how quantum collective behaviour emerges.
assessment.attribution: Bloch and Greiner (Mott transition and microscopy) and Esslinger (fermions, Fermi-Hubbard) are the principal experimentalists. Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) provided the proposal and is credited here, but I limit myself to three. Choosing among four credited names is a difficult allocation.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of replication in many laboratories, and the platform is mature. Quantum simulation of challenging models such as Fermi-Hubbard is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with B023 (Zoller, Cirac) means a prize could not honour both comfortably.
Four credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so someone is left out.
Relation to the 2001 BEC prize may be argued either way.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates, and the Innsbruck realisation of controlled gates and entangled-state engineering, provided the concrete route to quantum computation and simulation in atomic systems. Importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the theorists and Blatt a lead experimentalist, but Wineland (already a laureate) and Monroe also made decisive contributions. The overlap with the 2012 prize and the many-names issue complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: Gate fidelities and ion-trap processors have been confirmed by many groups for over two decades. The prize would be timely given the current progress in quantum technology.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize.
Overlap with B037 and B048 through Cirac and Zoller.
Technological motivation may weigh somewhat more than fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce protected edge states, a new state of matter distinguished by topology. Theory (Kane-Mele) and the HgTe observation by Molenkamp are an excellent theory-experiment pair.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele for the Z2 classification and Molenkamp for the experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect is a coherent trio. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe effect and Moore, Balents, Fu and Hasan also contributed, so the credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups in several materials over about fifteen years. It is partially covered by the 2016 prize (topological phases), so novelty relative to that prize may be questioned.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz prize.
Contested credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang).
My knowledge of condensed matter priority disputes is less secure than in AMO.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry uses matter-wave coherence for inertial sensing and tests of fundamental physics, including measurements of g and the fine-structure constant and tests of the equivalence principle. It directly probes how far quantum superposition extends to massive objects.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard (first atom interferometer), Bordé (theory of Ramsey-Bordé interferometry) and Kasevich (atomic fountain and precision gravimetry) are plausible. Chu (already a laureate) and Chebotayev, Mlynek and Keith also contributed, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: A mature field with commercial gravimeters and large-baseline projects; precision records have been reproduced by several groups. Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 prizes weakens the case a little.
uncertainties: Overlap with Chu's 1997 prize and the 2001 BEC prize.
Disputed early credit among the first interferometers (1991).
Priority ordering of Bordé's contribution is uncertain in my memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezing vacuum noise below the standard quantum limit shows concretely how quantum fluctuations can be shaped. Caves' proposal for interferometer squeezing, Kimble's early observation and the later use in gravitational-wave detectors give this fundamental and practical significance.
assessment.attribution: Caves (theory), Kimble (first experimental squeezing in the 1980s) and Schnabel (GEO600 and long-term development) form a defensible set. Walls, Slusher and Mavalvala (LIGO implementation) are credited or omitted in ways that make the allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Squeezed light is now routinely used in LIGO and Virgo, so the technique is confirmed. Because it supports the 2017 prize area it could be viewed as a refinement.
uncertainties: Omitting Mavalvala and Slusher is arguably unfair.
Overlap with 2017 LIGO prize and 2012 Haroche prize.
Four credited names exceed the three-laureate limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and is among the most important results in decades. The theory was recognised in 2013, and the discovery was a very large experimental achievement.
assessment.attribution: Spokespersons and founders of ATLAS and CMS can be credited for the experiments, but the discovery was by thousands, and the attribution to a few people is awkward. Whether a collaboration-based or an individual-based prize is appropriate remains unresolved. I defer to colleagues in particle physics here.
assessment.maturity: Both experiments confirmed the discovery independently, and many measurements of couplings have followed. The recognition would be late rather than premature, but the Nobel was already awarded for the theory.
uncertainties: Attribution to a few individuals in huge collaborations is difficult.
Choice of spokespersons versus other key leaders is uncertain.
My expertise in particle physics is limited.
